a: ab, ā (prep. + abl.) — from, away from; by (ā before consonants)
ab: ab, ā (prep. + abl.) — from, away from; by
ac: atque, ac — and, and also (ac before consonants)
acuto: acūtus, -a, -um — sharp, pointed, jagged (m./n. abl./dat. sg.)
ad: ad (prep. + acc.) — to, toward; at, near
aeneae: Aenēās, -ae (m.) — Aeneas, Trojan prince, son of Venus and Anchises (gen./dat. sg.)
aeolus: Aeolus, -ī (m.) — Aeolus, king and keeper of the winds (nom. sg.)
aequor: aequor, aequoris (n.) — level surface; the sea (acc./nom. sg.)
aequora: aequor, aequoris (n.) — level surface; the sea, the waters (acc./nom. pl.)
aequore: aequor, aequoris (n.) — level surface; the sea (abl. sg.)
alta: altus, -a, -um — high; deep (f. nom./abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
alto: altus, -a, -um — high; deep; altum (n.) as noun, the deep sea (abl./dat. sg.)
animis: animus, -ī (m.) — mind, spirit, heart; courage, temper (dat./abl. pl.)
animos: animus, -ī (m.) — mind, spirit; temper, passion (acc. pl.)
ante: ante (prep. + acc., adv.) — before, in front of; previously
arma: arma, -ōrum (n. pl.) — arms, weapons; war (acc./nom. pl.)
ast: ast (conj.) — but (archaic, solemn form of at)
aut: aut (conj.) — or; aut… aut, either… or
corripuit: corripiō, corripere, corripuī, correptum — to seize, snatch up (3rd sg. perf.)
cum: cum — (conj.) when, since, although; (prep. + abl.) with
dedit: dō, dare, dedī, datum — to give; to grant (+ inf.) (3rd sg. perf.)
est: sum, esse, fuī — to be (3rd sg. pres.); also forms perfect passives (ūsa est)
et: et — and; also, even; et… et: both… and
ex: ex, ē (prep. + abl.) — out of, from
fluctus: flūctus, -ūs (m.) — wave, billow (acc./nom. pl.; nom. sg.)
haec: hic, haec, hoc — this; haec (n. pl.), these things, these words (n. nom./acc. pl.; f. nom. sg.)
hic: hīc (adv.) — here; hic, haec, hoc (pron.), this (m. nom. sg.)
hinc: hinc (adv.) — from here, hence; from this
his: hic, haec, hoc — this; pl. these (dat./abl. pl.)
iam: iam (adv.) — now, already; iam… iam, now… now
ille: ille, illa, illud — that; he, that man (m. nom. sg.)
illi: ille, illa, illud — that; illī, they, those (m. nom. pl.); to him/her (dat. sg.)
in: in (prep.) — + acc. into, onto, against; + abl. in, on
ingens: ingēns, ingentis — huge, enormous, mighty (nom. sg.)
insequitur: īnsequor, īnsequī, īnsecūtus sum — to follow, follow on, come next (3rd sg. pres.)
ipsos: ipse, ipsa, ipsum — himself, herself, itself; the very (m. acc. pl.)
irae: īra, -ae (f.) — anger; pl. fits of anger, resentments (nom. pl.; gen./dat. sg.)
iunonis: Iūnō, Iūnōnis (f.) — Juno, queen of the gods (gen. sg.)
magno: magnus, -a, -um — great, large, loud (m./n. abl./dat. sg.)
meritis: meritum, -ī (n.) — service, merit, deserving deed (abl./dat. pl.)
mihi: ego, meī — I; mihi, to/for me (dat.)
murmure: murmur, murmuris (n.) — murmur, rumble, roar (abl. sg.)
nec: nec, neque — and not, nor; nec… nec, neither… nor
nubes: nūbēs, nūbis (f.) — cloud (nom./acc. pl.; nom. sg.)
numine: nūmen, nūminis (n.) — divine will, divinity, godhead (abl. sg.)
omnis: omnis, -e — all, every (acc. pl., = omnēs; also nom./gen. sg.)
per: per (prep. + acc.) — through, across, throughout; by
pietate: pietās, pietātis (f.) — devotion, sense of duty to gods, family and country (abl. sg.)
qua: quā (adv.) — where, by which way; in any way (after sī); also quī/quis, f. abl. sg.
quae: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel., f. nom. sg.; f./n. nom./acc. pl.)
quam: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel., f. acc. sg.); quam (adv.), how; than
quem: quī, quae, quod — who, whom (rel. or interrog., m. acc. sg.)
sed: sed (conj.) — but; sed enim, but indeed
sic: sīc (adv.) — so, thus, in this way
sidera: sīdus, sīderis (n.) — star, constellation; pl. the sky (acc./nom. pl.)
sub: sub (prep.) — + abl. under, beneath; + acc. up to, under
talia: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind; tālia, such things, such words (n. acc./nom. pl.)
temperat: temperō, -āre — to moderate, restrain, temper (3rd sg. pres.)
tollere: tollō, tollere, sustulī, sublātum — to lift, raise (pres. inf.)
troas: Trōs, Trōis (m.) — a Trojan (acc. pl., Greek form Trōas)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
unam: ūnus, -a, -um — one, one alone, single (f. acc. sg.)
vasto: vastus, -a, -um — vast, huge, desolate (m./n. abl./dat. sg.)
virum: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero (acc. sg.; also gen. pl., old form = virōrum)
